How a developer frees RAM by hand before simulator or emulator debugging, with the scripts of this repository. Run it only
when nobody is debugging on a simulator or emulator: it quits apps and restarts simulators.

| Platform | Script | Section |
|:---|:---|:---|
| macOS | [release-ram.sh](../release-ram.sh), with [release-ram-restart-simulators.sh](../scripts/release-ram-restart-simulators.sh) and [release-ram-mirror-displays.swift](../scripts/release-ram-mirror-displays.swift) | [macOS](#macos) |
| Windows | [release-ram.ps1](../release-ram.ps1) | [Windows](#windows) |

This is not [free-ram.sh](../scripts/free-ram.sh): that script only flushes the disk cache and never quits an app or a
simulator, and AI agents run it before every simulator use. `release-ram.sh` quits things.

## The task these scripts do

Both sections come from this owner task (English, recorded 2026-11-26). Whoever runs it as an AI session finishes it by
messaging every Windows and macOS session.

> I am sure no simulator is being debugged. Close the following processes, and when done send a message to all sessions
> on Windows and macOS: "the simulators were restarted; if you are waiting for a simulator to debug, start simulator
> debugging again". Close the WeChat mini program tool and the HarmonyOS emulator, close React Native watchman, close
> Gradle, close Obsidian, close Android Studio, close the Android emulator, close Chrome, close all Finder windows.
> Close inactive simulators; inactive means no session is debugging on the simulator; let inactive simulators sleep or
> shut them down. Close bionic, opencode and MiniMax Code. Close TextExpander. Turn the brightness of all displays down
> to almost black.
>
> This insert is the macOS section: close CleanMyMac, the WeChat mini program tool and the HarmonyOS IDE, the HarmonyOS
> emulator, Gradle, Obsidian, Xcode, Android Studio, the Android emulator and Chrome; restart Finder and close all Finder
> windows. Close inactive simulators (no session is debugging on them). Restart the iOS simulators and keep at most two.
> Let inactive simulators sleep or shut them down. Show multiple displays mirrored. Reduce transparency of the operating
> system. Hide all iTerm2 windows and keep it active in the background.

The first paragraph is the Windows section, the second the macOS section.

## macOS

1. Make sure nobody debugs on a simulator.
2. Open a terminal in the repository root and look first (changes nothing):

   ```sh
   ./release-ram.sh --dry-run
   ```

3. Run it. It asks you to type `yes` (or pass `--yes`). Name the simulators to restart and keep, at most two:

   ```sh
   ./release-ram.sh --yes --keep <UDID> --keep <UDID>
   ```

   `xcrun simctl list devices booted` shows the UDIDs. Without `--keep` the two most recently used booted simulators are
   restarted.
4. Tell every Windows and macOS session that the simulators were restarted (see "The task").

What it does, in order. Run one step with `--only name`, leave one out with `--skip name`:

| Step | What happens |
|:---|:---|
| `apps` | Quits CleanMyMac, the WeChat mini program tool, DevEco Studio, Obsidian, Xcode, Android Studio and Chrome (a polite quit, then a kill after 6 s); `adb emu kill` for every Android emulator, then the emulator processes; the HarmonyOS emulator by name (best effort: the DevEco binary names change between releases). `--extra "App Name"` quits one more app. |
| `gradle` | Stops the Gradle daemons. |
| `simulators` | [release-ram-restart-simulators.sh](../scripts/release-ram-restart-simulators.sh): restarts the named simulators by force and keeps at most two. See below. |
| `finder` | Closes every Finder window, then restarts Finder. |
| `displays` | [release-ram-mirror-displays.swift](../scripts/release-ram-mirror-displays.swift) mirrors every display onto the main one for the login session (`swift scripts/release-ram-mirror-displays.swift --off` undoes it). |
| `transparency` | `defaults write com.apple.universalaccess reduceTransparency -bool true`; if macOS refuses, set System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Reduce transparency by hand. |
| `iterm` | Hides the iTerm2 windows through System Events; iTerm2 keeps running. If macOS refuses, give your terminal the Accessibility permission or press Cmd+H in iTerm2. |

### Restarting a simulator that is occupied

`scripts/release-ram-restart-simulators.sh --udid <UDID>` works when a plain `simctl shutdown` hangs, for example a
stuck boot, a running app, `xcodebuild` or `xctest` on the device, or a device stuck in "Shutting Down":

1. `simctl shutdown <UDID>` with a timeout (default 90 s, `--timeout`).
2. If the device is not shut down: the processes whose command line names the UDID (`launchd_sim`, test runners, `simctl`
   helpers) get SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s. Never the script itself or its parents.
3. `simctl shutdown <UDID>` again.
4. Only with `--allow-service-restart`: CoreSimulatorService is restarted. That service is shared, so every simulator of
   the Mac stops; use it only as the last resort.
5. `simctl boot <UDID>`, then `simctl bootstatus <UDID> -b` until it is booted (`--no-boot` stops after the shutdown).

Rules it keeps: it never runs `simctl shutdown all`; every device is named by its UDID; a booted simulator that is not named
is **left alone** unless you pass `--shutdown-others` (a script cannot know whether another session is testing on it).
At most two simulators are kept (`--keep-max`).

Run it alone:

```sh
scripts/release-ram-restart-simulators.sh --udid <UDID> --dry-run   # look first
scripts/release-ram-restart-simulators.sh --udid <UDID>             # restart by force
```

Tested on 2026-11-26 (macOS 27.3, Xcode 27.2, one throwaway iPhone 18 Pro simulator created for the test): the device was
booted, Settings was running on it, a process named its UDID, and its `launchd_sim` was frozen with `kill -STOP`, so
`simctl shutdown` hung (killed by a 5 s probe, exit 142). The script shut it down, started it again and it reached Booted
in 37 s to 67 s, twice. The other booted simulator stayed booted after the fix below.

> Lesson of the first test run (2026-11-26): the first version shut down every booted simulator that was not named, and
> it stopped another session's simulator. It was booted again at once and that session was told. Shutting down unnamed
> simulators is now opt-in (`--shutdown-others`).

## Windows

1. Make sure nobody debugs on an emulator.
2. Open PowerShell in the repository root and look first (changes nothing):

   ```powershell
   .\release-ram.ps1 -DryRun
   ```

3. Run it. It asks you to type `yes` (or pass `-Yes`). Name the Android emulators to keep:

   ```powershell
   .\release-ram.ps1 -Yes -KeepEmulator emulator-5556
   ```

4. Tell every Windows and macOS session that the emulators were restarted (see "The task").

Steps (`-Only name,name`, `-Skip name`): `apps` (WeChat DevTools, DevEco Studio, the HarmonyOS emulator, Obsidian, Android
Studio, Chrome, bionic, opencode, MiniMax Code, TextExpander; `-Extra name` adds one process), `watchman`, `gradle`,
`explorer` (closes the Explorer windows, taskbar and desktop stay), `emulators` (`adb emu kill` for every Android emulator
that is not named in `-KeepEmulator`) and `brightness` (the built-in display through WMI, `-Brightness 1` is the percent;
external monitors have no WMI brightness, lower them with their buttons).

Status: the Windows script was written on a Mac and **not run yet**. A Windows session runs `.\release-ram.ps1 -DryRun`
first and reports what it prints; the process names of the HarmonyOS emulator, bionic and MiniMax Code are guesses to
check there.
